title: introduce-telemetry-stitcher-and-kernel-warmup-profiling
author: Lena Wu
description:
Motivation: We see recurring gaps between sampled traces and the low-level kernel warmup events that cause early bursts of GPU occupancy and token-cost variance for short inputs. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) a lightweight Telemetry Stitcher that correlates sampled spans with sparse kernel warmup traces and async prefetch events; and 2) Kernel Warmup Profiling meters that surface warmup duration, first-token-latency delta, and warmup-trigger fingerprints per model variant.

What this PR does: Adds a Telemetry Stitcher service in the runtime that attaches compact context hashes to spans when available, performs best-effort enrichment of existing sampled traces with kernel-warmup fingerprints, and emits a compact warmup profile metric family (labels: model, quantization, seq_len_bucket, warmup_type). Also introduces Grafana dashboards (compact warmup heatmap + per-route first-token-delta panel), a new Prometheus exporter endpoint for warmup metrics, and a small SDK helper in the tracing instrumentation to propagate the stitcher context key.

Design notes: The stitcher is intentionally opportunistic and non-blocking; it writes a 128-bit base64 fingerprint to span attributes when it can reconcile kernel warmup events with invocation metadata. To avoid cardinality explosion we: (a) downsample fingerprint labels via an LRU-capped hashing window, (b) expose only three seq_len_buckets for metric rollups, and (c) rely on controlled sampling policies for high-cardinality routes. Warmup profiling uses reservoir sampling with a capped cardinality tag-set and emits aggregated histograms to minimize ingestion costs.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.telemetry.stitcher (default off for Hosted for 2 weeks). We will enable in Dedicated non-critical cluster for 48 hours, validate dashboards and stepwise increase sampling. Manual kill switch in console and an autosuppress flow if metric cardinality exceeds thresholds.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the stitcher context propagation added in redwood/serving/runtime/tracing/test_stitcher.py. E2E replay bench included that replays synthetic kernels to validate warmup-to-span correlations. Added integration test that asserts warmup metrics presence in the exporter after 100 synthetic short-invocation runs. Load test at scale was run on staging (summary in CI checks).

Migration notes: No data migrations. New metrics will appear with the warmup_ prefix and will be opt-in. SDK change is backward compatible; spans without the stitcher context are unaffected.

Related work: complements ENG-1482 (adaptive batching warmup mitigation) and ENG-1499 (token-cost attribution). Incident SUP-3421 prompted the initial investigation (root cause: fast short requests triggering kernel JIT warmup bursts).

Risks: Potential metric cardinality growth (mitigations above) and slight additional CPU usage in the runtime (<1% median p99 on staging observed).

Action items post-merge: Enable runtime flag for one Dedicated non-prod pool, validate dashboards for 72 hours, and file follow-ups for long-term agreggation (ENG-1527).
